label: This accolade
summary: The accolade currently in focus in the interface, handed on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it as the argument of other functions, for example one that picks a portrait pose and one that gives a text about which knights suit an accolade type. Going by its name and these uses, it stands for the accolade itself.

label: This selection window
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the accolade attribute selection window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name appears on other types, where it is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Close selection window
summary: Closes the window where a new attribute for an accolade is chosen.
details: Vanilla runs it from click handlers in the accolade attribute selection window.

label: Confirm selection
summary: Confirms the attribute type that was picked in the accolade attribute selection window.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click handler in that window. Going by its name and this use, it applies the chosen attribute.

label: Accolade
summary: Returns the accolade the attribute selection window is about.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of that window, so the widgets inside can show the accolade's data.

label: All attributes
summary: Going by its name, returns every attribute that can be chosen for the accolade; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered and the input shows no use of it.

label: Available attributes
summary: Going by its name, returns the attributes that can currently be chosen; the game documents nothing more.
details: The return type is not registered and the input shows no use of it.

label: Other attributes
summary: Returns a list of the other attribute types, used to fill a list in the selection window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in the accolade attribute selection window. What exactly makes an attribute count as other is not stated; going by its name, it is the rest apart from the selected one.

label: Selected attribute type
summary: Returns the accolade type (attribute) that is currently selected in the selection window.
details: Vanilla compares it with each listed type to show that row as pressed and visible, and uses it as the data context of another part of the window.

label: Select attribute type
summary: Reacts to a click on an accolade type in the selection window; it takes the clicked type.
details: Vanilla calls it with the accolade type of the clicked row. Going by its name, it makes that type the selected one.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The accolade type that was clicked.
fields.values: an accolade type, such as AccoladeType.Self

label: This selection window
summary: Going by its name, the accolade attribute selection window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: This history entry
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the accolade history entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Acclaimed date
summary: The date on which a knight became the acclaimed knight in this history entry.
details: Vanilla prints it with GetString in the history line "Became the acclaimed knight on ...".

label: Acclaimed knight
summary: The knight who was the acclaimed knight in this history entry.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data context of a part of the accolade window, so that part can show that knight.

label: This history entry
summary: Going by its name, the accolade history entry itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: This rank
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the accolade rank itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Rank effects
summary: Returns the text describing what this accolade rank gives.
details: Vanilla shows it in the tooltip of a rank, under the line with the rank's level and glory.

label: This rank
summary: The accolade rank currently in focus, handed on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to functions that give the level, or the level and glory, of a rank.

label: This accolade type
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the accolade type itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Build effects text
summary: Going by its name, returns a text built from the effects of this accolade type.
details: Vanilla shows it in the tooltip for choosing an accolade type (in one place followed by the hint that a click chooses it).

label: Custom text
summary: Going by its name, returns a custom text of the accolade type, picked by a name you give.
details: The input shows no use on this type. The same name on other types takes a text name in quotes, for example Character.Custom('...'), and returns the matching custom localization text.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the custom text.

label: Icon
summary: Returns the icon picture of this accolade type.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture in the attribute selection window and the create accolade window.

label: Knight suits type
summary: Going by its name, checks whether a knight suits this accolade type; the game documents nothing more.
details: It takes two arguments and returns true or false. The input shows no use of it. The related function GetKnightValidForAccoladeTypeDesc gives the explaining text.

label: Why knight suits type
summary: Going by its name, returns a text about whether the knight of the given accolade suits this accolade type.
details: Vanilla checks whether this text is empty: if not, it adds the text to the type's tooltip, and it also adds the text to the tooltip of the disabled attribute selection.

label: Level and glory of rank
summary: Returns a text with the level and the glory of the given rank of this accolade type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the heading of a rank tooltip, with the rank passed in.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an accolade rank, such as AccoladeRank.Self

label: Level of rank
summary: Returns a text with the level of the given rank of this accolade type.
details: Vanilla uses it in a tooltip, with the rank passed in.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an accolade rank, such as AccoladeRank.Self

label: Men-at-arms unlock
summary: Going by its name, returns the men-at-arms unlock of this accolade type.
details: Vanilla checks it with IsValid to show a part of the create accolade window only when it is valid, and uses it as the data context of that part. Men-at-arms are the soldier regiments a ruler can hire.

label: Men-at-arms unlock warning
summary: Going by its name, returns a warning text about the men-at-arms unlock of this accolade type; the game documents nothing more.
details: It returns text and takes no arguments. The input shows no use of it.

label: Name
summary: Returns the name of this accolade type, as text.
details: Vanilla uses it in the accolade window and in the line "gains the ... attribute". Going by its name, the related GetNameNoTooltip gives the name without the tooltip that this one carries.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: Returns the name of this accolade type as plain text, without a tooltip.
details: Vanilla uses it as a text in the attribute selection window, the create accolade window and a shared tooltip.

label: Name with accolade
summary: Returns the name of this accolade type, taking an accolade into account.
details: Only a use on a related path is shown: the upgrade tooltip calls it on the type of an obtained accolade, passing Accolade.Self. What the accolade changes in the name is not stated.

label: Pose
summary: Going by its name, returns the portrait pose of this accolade type; the game documents nothing more.
details: It returns text and takes no arguments. The input shows no use of it.

label: Ranks
summary: Returns the list of ranks of this accolade type.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in a shared tooltip, one row per rank.

label: Is valid
summary: Going by its name, whether this accolade type exists and is usable.
details: Returns true or false. The input shows no use on this type; the same name is used on other types to test that a value exists.

label: This accolade type
summary: The accolade type of the current row, handed on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the click handlers that select a type, in the attribute selection window and the create accolade window.

label: Military view
summary: Gives access to the military view, used as the data context in the accolade window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the accolade window. What the military view holds is not stated.

label: This accolade view
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the accolade window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Clear successor
summary: Going by its name, removes the chosen successor of the accolade; the game documents nothing more.
details: Returns nothing. The input shows no use of it.

label: Close accolade window
summary: Closes the accolade window.
details: Vanilla runs it from click handlers in that window.

label: Edit name
summary: Called when the text in the accolade's name field is edited.
details: Vanilla uses it as the handler for edited text in a field of the accolade window.

label: Accolade
summary: Returns the accolade shown in the accolade window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in several places of that window so the parts can show the accolade's data.

label: Squire quality
summary: Returns a text about the quality of the accolade's squires.
details: Vanilla shows it after the label for the accolade's squires.

label: Squire quality breakdown
summary: Returns a text that explains how the squire quality is made up.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the accolade window.

label: Number of traits
summary: Going by its name, returns how many traits the accolade window lists; the game documents nothing more.
details: Returns a whole number. The input shows no use of it. GetTraits is the list itself.

label: Progress bar
summary: Returns the progress bar data of the accolade window.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in that window. Going by its name, it feeds a progress bar.

label: Temporary name
summary: Returns the name typed so far in the rename field, before it is saved.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the accolade window. Going by its name and the renaming functions next to it, it is the name being edited.

label: Traits
summary: Returns the list of traits shown in the accolade window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of a list in that window.

label: Has relevant traits
summary: Whether there are any traits relevant to the accolade to show.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the accolade window only when it is true. Which traits count as relevant is not stated.

label: Is renaming
summary: Whether the accolade is currently being renamed.
details: Vanilla shows the name field when it is true and the plain name when it is not.

label: Is showing history
summary: Whether the accolade window currently shows the history of acclaimed knights.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the history part of the window.

label: Level up type
summary: Levels up the given obtained accolade type.
details: Vanilla calls it from a click handler in the accolade window, passing the obtained accolade type of that row.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The obtained accolade type to level up.
fields.values: an obtained accolade type, such as ObtainedAccoladeType.Self

label: Open attribute selection
summary: Opens the window where a new attribute for the accolade is chosen.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click in the accolade window.

label: This accolade view
summary: Going by its name, the accolade window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Set acclaimed knight
summary: Going by its name, sets the acclaimed knight of the accolade to the given one; the game documents nothing more.
details: Returns nothing and takes one argument. The input shows no use of it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by its name, the knight.

label: Set successor
summary: Going by its name, sets the successor of the accolade to the given one; the game documents nothing more.
details: Returns nothing and takes one argument. The input shows no use of it.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; going by its name, the successor.

label: Submit name
summary: Saves the new name typed for the accolade.
details: Vanilla runs it when the return key is pressed in the name field of the accolade window.

label: Toggle history
summary: Switches the accolade window between showing the history and not showing it.
details: Vanilla runs it from clicks in that window; IsShowingHistory reports the state.

label: Toggle renaming
summary: Switches the accolade between being renamed and not.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click in the accolade window; IsRenaming reports the state.

label: This inventory
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the account inventory itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. The game's documentation files it under the GUI category.

label: Has item
summary: Whether the Paradox account's inventory holds the given item.
details: The engine's account GUI shows one element when the inventory has been fetched and holds the item, and another when it does not. Vanilla passes the item's name as text, `'in_game_item'`.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: an item name as text, such as 'in_game_item'

label: Inventory loaded
summary: Whether the Paradox account's inventory has been fetched yet.
details: The engine's account GUI shows one element while it has not, and checks it before asking whether an item is held.

label: This inventory
summary: Going by its name, the account inventory itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: This achievement
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the achievement itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Is unlocked
summary: Going by its name, whether the achievement is unlocked.
details: Returns true or false. A line in the frontend uses it after an achievement lookup to decide whether something is visible; that line is a hint from a path of another type.

label: This achievement
summary: Going by its name, the achievement itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Just unlocked achievements
summary: Returns the list of achievements that were just unlocked, for the achievement popup.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the list in the popup.

label: This popup
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the achievement popup itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: This popup
summary: Going by its name, the achievement popup itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Show popup window
summary: Going by its name, opens the achievement popup window.
details: Returns nothing. The one line in the input is another type's ShowWindow, so no use of this exact function is shown.

label: Achievement groups
summary: Returns the groups of achievements shown in the achievement window.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the list in that window.

label: This achievement window
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the achievement window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Has game started
summary: Whether a game has been started, as the achievement window sees it.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to show or hide parts of the achievement window. Going by its name, it separates opening the window in a running game from opening it elsewhere.

label: Hide window
summary: Closes (hides) the achievement window.
details: Vanilla runs it from click handlers in that window.

label: This achievement window
summary: Going by its name, the achievement window itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Showing all
summary: Whether the window currently shows all achievements.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the all filter button as pressed and to change how a part reacts to the mouse.

label: Showing locked
summary: Whether the window currently shows only locked achievements.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the locked filter button as pressed. Going by its name, locked means not yet unlocked.

label: Showing possible
summary: Whether the window currently shows only the possible achievements.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the possible filter button as pressed. What makes an achievement possible is not stated.

label: Showing unlocked
summary: Whether the window currently shows only the unlocked achievements.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the unlocked filter button as pressed.

label: Show window
summary: Going by its name, opens the achievement window.
details: Returns nothing. The line in the input belongs to another type, so no use of this exact function is shown.

label: Show all
summary: Makes the achievement window list all achievements.
details: Vanilla runs it from the all filter button.

label: Show locked
summary: Makes the achievement window list only the locked achievements.
details: Vanilla runs it from the locked filter button.

label: Show possible
summary: Makes the achievement window list only the possible achievements.
details: Vanilla runs it from the possible filter button.

label: Show unlocked
summary: Makes the achievement window list only the unlocked achievements.
details: Vanilla runs it from the unlocked filter button.

label: This action item handler
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the action item handler itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Actions went up
summary: Whether the number of action items has gone up.
details: Vanilla uses it as a trigger condition of notification animations in the HUD. Going by its name, an animation plays when new actions appear.

label: Action items
summary: Returns the list of action items shown in the HUD notification part.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the action list in the notification part of the HUD.

label: Number of actions
summary: Going by its name, returns how many action items there are; the game documents nothing more.
details: Returns a whole number. The input shows no use of it.

label: Unread actions
summary: Returns how many action items have not been read yet.
details: Vanilla shows the number in the HUD and in the tooltip "You have N unread messages".

label: Suggestions debug text
summary: Returns a debug text about the suggestions, appended to the actions tooltip.
details: Vanilla adds it to the end of the tips tooltip. Going by its name, it is meant for debugging.

label: Has actions
summary: Going by its name, whether any action items are available; the game documents nothing more.
details: Returns true or false. The input shows no use of it.

label: Has current situation items
summary: Whether there are action items about the current situation.
details: Vanilla uses it, and its negation, to switch between two views in the HUD notification list.

label: Has dangerous action
summary: Whether a visible action item is marked as dangerous.
details: Vanilla uses it to show a part of the HUD notification only when it is true.

label: Is list visible
summary: Whether the action item list is currently open.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the list in the HUD. ToggleList opens and closes it.

label: Mark all as read
summary: Marks all action items as read.
details: Vanilla runs it from a button click in the HUD notification part. GetNumberOfUnreadActions gives the unread count.

label: Reset dismissed
summary: Brings back the action items that were dismissed.
details: Vanilla runs it from a click in the HUD. Going by its name, dismissed items show again.

label: This action item handler
summary: Going by its name, the action item handler itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Should be visible
summary: Going by its name, whether the action items part should be shown.
details: Returns true or false. The line in the input belongs to another type (the top bar), so no use of this exact function is shown.

label: Toggle list
summary: Opens or closes the action item list.
details: Vanilla runs it from clicks in the HUD; IsListVisible reports the state.

label: This activity option
summary: Gives access to the active activity option itself, handed to another function.
details: Vanilla passes it to the function that switches editing of an option in the activity planner.

label: Category
summary: Returns the category this activity option belongs to.
details: Vanilla reads its name, its list of options and its icon in the activity planner, for example in "(category Level N)" in a tooltip.

label: Option
summary: Returns the activity option behind this active option.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context and reads its index in the category from it, which is shown as a level number.

label: This activity option
summary: Going by its name, the active activity option itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: This casus belli
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the active casus belli (war reason) itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Attacker
summary: Going by its name, the character who attacks with this casus belli (war reason).
details: A line in a war text uses it as a character on the war's active casus belli; that line is a hint from another path.

label: Defender
summary: Going by its name, the character who defends against this casus belli (war reason).
details: A line in a war text uses it as a character on the war's active casus belli; that line is a hint from another path.

label: First title target
summary: Going by its name, the first title that the casus belli targets; the game documents nothing more.
details: The input shows no use of it.

label: Casus belli type
summary: Going by its name, the type of this casus belli (war reason).
details: The line in the input is another type's GetType, so no use of this exact function is shown.

label: This casus belli
summary: Going by its name, the active casus belli itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: This council task
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the active council task itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Can be fired
summary: Going by its name, whether the councillor of this task can be dismissed; the game documents nothing more.
details: Returns true or false. The input shows no use of it.

label: Can be reassigned
summary: Going by its name, whether this task can be given to someone else.
details: Returns true or false. The line in the input belongs to another type, so no use of this exact function is shown.

label: Councillor
summary: Returns the councillor who has this task.
details: Vanilla reads the councillor's name in council texts and uses the councillor as a data context in the council task view.

label: Court owner
summary: The ruler whose council the task belongs to.
details: Vanilla's texts about choosing the next councillor use it: "... will be next [position] for [court owner]". The game gives no return type, but the texts read a name from it.

label: Time left
summary: Returns a text with the estimated time until the task is done.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the council window and in a value breakdown. ETA is short for estimated time of arrival.

label: Location
summary: Going by its name, the place where the task happens.
details: The line in the input is another type's GetLocation, so no use of this exact function is shown.

label: Task name
summary: The council task's name, as text.
details: Vanilla's one use is a message: "... can no longer continue with [task]".

label: Next forced councillor
summary: Going by its name, the councillor who is next in line to be forced into this position.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the council window. What forced means here is not stated.

label: Position name
summary: Returns the name of the council position this task belongs to.
details: Vanilla uses it in texts such as "Click to appoint a ..." and as text in the council task view.

label: Position name, possessive
summary: The name of the council position doing the task, in its possessive form.
details: Vanilla's one use: "Your [position's] current Task (...) will be aborted". The game spells the name Possesive, with one s.

label: Position tooltip
summary: Returns the tooltip text of the council position.
details: Vanilla uses it as a tooltip in the council window.

label: Position type
summary: Returns the council position type of this task.
details: Vanilla reads the player-facing name from it in texts and uses it as a data context in the council views.

label: Progress
summary: Returns how far the task has progressed, as a number.
details: Vanilla shows it as a percentage in some texts and next to the maximum in the progress tooltip.

label: Progress breakdown
summary: Returns the breakdown of how the task's progress is made up.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in a shared value breakdown view.

label: Progress (float)
summary: Returns the task's progress as a decimal number for a progress bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of progress bars in the council window and in shared components.

label: Progress needed
summary: Returns the progress the task needs to be done.
details: Vanilla shows it after the current progress in the progress tooltip.

label: Progress needed (float)
summary: Returns the progress the task needs, as a decimal number for a progress bar.
details: Vanilla uses it as the maximum of the progress bar in the council window.

label: Progress pie
summary: Returns the task's progress as a value for a pie-shaped indicator.
details: Vanilla uses it as the value of an icon on the map. Going by its name, the pie fills as the task advances.

label: Task scopes
summary: Returns the scope data of the task, which vanilla hands to the task type's effect description.
details: Vanilla passes it to the task type's effect description function for a tooltip in the council window. What it holds exactly is not stated.

label: Target court
summary: Going by its name, the court the task is aimed at; the game documents nothing more.
details: The input shows no use of it.

label: Target province
summary: Going by its name, the province the task is aimed at; the game documents nothing more.
details: The input shows no use of it.

label: Task asset
summary: Returns the asset (art) of the task, which gives the task's icon.
details: Vanilla reads its task icon for the map icon layer.

label: Task effect
summary: Returns the text describing what the task does.
details: Vanilla shows it under an "Effects" heading in the council window.

label: Task target
summary: Returns a text naming what the task is aimed at.
details: Vanilla shows it as text in the council window.

label: Task type
summary: Returns the council task type of this task.
details: Vanilla reads the type's name in council texts.

label: Task type or default
summary: Returns the council task type, or a default type when there is none.
details: Vanilla uses it as a data context in the council window. The default is not stated; the meaning rests on the name.

label: Task value name
summary: Returns the name of the value the task's progress is counted in.
details: Vanilla shows it in the progress tooltip heading, right after the progress and maximum numbers.

label: Has councillor
summary: Whether a councillor is assigned to this task.
details: Vanilla combines it with HasMainSkill to decide when to show a part of the council window.

label: Has main skill
summary: Whether the task has a main skill that matters for it.
details: Vanilla uses it to show the skill parts of the council window and task view only when it is true.

label: Is frozen
summary: Whether the task is frozen, so it makes no progress.
details: Vanilla uses it on map icons to show a different look for frozen tasks. A council text says a character must be assigned to the position to continue.

label: Is valid
summary: Going by its name, whether this council task exists and is usable.
details: Returns true or false. The input shows no use on this type; the same name is used on other types to test that a value exists.

label: Make scope
summary: Going by its name and return type, turns the council task into a scope that script-side functions can work on.
details: The lines in the input belong to other types, so no use of this exact function is shown. There the same name is followed by ScriptValue(...), as in GetPlayer.MakeScope.ScriptValue('...').

label: This council task
summary: The active council task of the current row, handed on to other functions.
details: Vanilla passes it to the click handler of a task icon on the map.

label: This task icon
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the council task map icon itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Tasks
summary: Returns the council tasks shown by this map icon.
details: Vanilla uses it as the data model of the task list in the map icon layer.

label: On click
summary: Going by its name, reacts to a click on the task icon; it takes one argument.
details: Returns nothing. The line in the input is another type's OnClick, so no use of this exact function is shown. What the argument is, is not stated.

label: This task icon
summary: Going by its name, the council task map icon itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to hand the current item to another function. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: This activity
summary: Going by its name, gives access to the activity itself; the game documents nothing more.
details: The same name on other types is used to pass a widget along. Nothing in the input shows this exact function in use.

label: Add character to phase group
summary: Adds a character to a named group (such as spectators or contestants) for one phase of the activity.
details: Vanilla calls it from the tournament window with the phase, the player and the group name 'spectator' or 'contestant'.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a planned phase, such as PlannedActivityPhase.Self

fields.name: Arg2
fields.values: a quoted name, such as 'spectator' or 'contestant'

label: Add character to group
summary: Adds a character to a named group of the activity, such as spectators.
details: Vanilla calls it from the tournament knight list with a character and the group name 'spectator'.

label: Estimated travel time
summary: Returns the estimated travel time to the activity, as a whole number (days, going by its use).
details: Vanilla uses it in the "Travel time estimate" text of the activity list window, passed through GetTimeDifferenceWithDays; the unit rests on that use. Vanilla passes the player's character as the argument.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: Not documented; vanilla passes the player's character.
